scope: Structural canonical-source migration with exact whole-corpus and delivery parity.
ownershipDecisions: Every record has an explicit canonical owner and ordered ID in the manifest.
Dossiers received an authoring home in their first listed chapter during migration. Existing chapter memberships remain in each full record.
A single source registry owns access dates, citations' target identities and scope limits.
Cross-chapter journeys, comparisons, relationships and glossary terms have a shared owner.
The compiler obtains a fresh canonical corpus on every invocation. The historical 35-stage pipeline is retained for provenance and comparison.

verification.c1Pilot: The actual C1 canonical file replaced its records in the historical assembly. All whole-corpus bytes and 190 delivery JSON files matched the frozen inputs.
verification.allChapters: The canonical loader joined all eight chapters, sources and shared records using manifest order. All whole-corpus bytes and 190 delivery JSON files matched the same frozen inputs.
verification.repeatability: Repeated default compilation reproduced delivery bytes. Independent assembly and nested-record mutation isolation passed.
verification.negativeContracts: Focused regressions reject duplicate, missing, unowned and misplaced records, contradictory ownership/order entries and unsupported collections.

futureEditorialChanges: Canonical edits require current delivery/citation validation and an explicitly recorded new corpus revision. The historical migration hash and field-writer history remain frozen. The ownership script compares a historical baseline only when ATLAS_BASELINE_CORPUS is explicitly supplied.
